## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results in this search yet. The earlier searches ran 84 trials, and every one scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, so the agent never finished an exact build. That points to optimisation and inductive bias, not generalisation. It is not known what changed in this world, so every candidate reads its sizes from spec and keeps its heads flexible. Two candidates add learned offset or dense per-action terms in case the anchor semantics differ from the description. Following the program, this round tries six very different stacks rather than refinements. All six use initialisation hygiene: orthogonal init, policy-logit gain 0.01 and value gain 1. They are combined with normalisation, factorised logits, a raw-observation skip, a weight-shared per-layer landing head, multi-scale context and recipe extremes not tried before (lr 3e-3, gamma 0.995, gae_lambda 0.99, clip 0.3, long rollouts with 1–2 epochs). Compute ratio is kept at about 1.0–1.3. Any nonzero score will be followed up in the next rounds.

### Round 2
All six round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and on training success. So did 84 earlier trials across 7 changed worlds. Round 1 combined init hygiene, GroupNorm, factorised logits, a raw-obs skip, global context, offset-robust heads and recipe extremes (lr 3e-3, 1 epoch at about 311k steps, gamma 0.995, clip 0.3). None of it helped. Because training success is also 0, the agent never completes an exact build. One explanation fits all of these failures: the unstated change breaks the alignment that conv nets take for granted, either between build and target, or between observation cells and action anchors (a flip, transpose, scramble or footprint swap). Local inductive biases cannot learn such a non-local remap. This round bets on learnable global remapping: MLP-Mixer token mixing, dihedral feature stacking, and a flattened-obs decoder. It adds two other bets: soft attention over each column's layers, and a big CNN trained for 1 epoch. Every slot is stacked and the six differ substantially.

### Round 3
All 12 trials in this search scored 0 on both dev and training success, like the 84 before them. Every trial trained without problems, so this is a learning failure, not a crash. The remap-robust designs (mixer, flattened decoder, dihedral, dense heads), per-layer and landing-layer heads, and recipe extremes such as lr 3e-3, 1 epoch and gamma 0.995 all failed. A simple remap or a pure optimisation setting is therefore unlikely to be the fix. Three things have not been tried yet:
- a head kernel learned over the exact footprint plus a one-cell border, so each anchor keeps exact per-cell detail instead of pooled summaries;
- capacity well above r=1.9;
- other structural biases: weight-tied iterative propagation, multiplicative two-stream features, every type pooling over every footprint shape (robust to a type permutation), and count-preserving sum pooling for DONE.

This round covers these, paired with different recipe regimes: short-horizon large batch, cheapest net with maximum samples, and 1 epoch with a big net. With everything at 0, breadth still matters more than refining any one candidate.

### Round 4
All 18 trials in this search scored 0 on dev and also on training success, and so did the 84 trials in earlier worlds. None of these ideas helped: init hygiene, normalisation, raw skips, factorised or dense heads, footprint-kernel heads, remap-robust heads (dihedral, mixer, flat), heads that pool every footprint shape, attention or count features for DONE, bilinear stems, weight-tied propagation, and recipe extremes (lr 3e-3, 1 epoch with 426k steps, gamma 0.9 to 0.995, clip 0.3, 1024 envs). Since training success is also 0, the agent never completes an exact build, so the problem is inductive bias, not generalisation. One structure no earlier trial built in: a learned landing height per footprint (a max-pool of a learned height map) that selects the per-layer features at that layer and the layers below it. That is what correctness and sealing depend on. This is the last round, and a score above 0 is needed for selection, so all six candidates use this landing-gated head.
